research.job_description_summary: LTIMindtree hires freshers mainly as Graduate Engineer Trainees (GET), with higher-paid tracks mentioned in secondary sources. A 2026 on-campus account and guides describe an online assessment of about three hours (aptitude, pseudocode and output prediction, OOP, language, DBMS, OS, networks and a voice assessment), a technical interview and an HR interview. The official careers site was not fetched for process details.
limitations: The official LTIMindtree careers site was not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED; rounds come from a 2026 LeetCode Discuss account (a secondhand account written by another person on behalf of a candidate, with no date visible) and two guides.
All class B items trace to that one account and carry times_reported 1 and low confidence.

The placementpreparation.io page says 'recent candidate reports' but attributes nothing to individuals, and its title says 2026 while a heading says 2025; its items (including the rice mixture, probability and relation puzzles) are treated as topic context and rebuilt as original practice items (class D).
Only the Graduate Engineer Trainee role is supported by sources; higher-band tracks are named only as 'up to 6.5 LPA' by a guide, so no separate track bank was created.
The reported 24 selected out of 600 candidates is a single-account figure and was not used.
Online-assessment length (about 3 hours versus 130 minutes and about 111 MCQs) differs between sources.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.

questions.prompt: What is the virtual DOM, and what is React Fiber?
questions.relevance_to_role: A 2026 on-campus account lists the virtual DOM and Fiber in the technical interview.
questions.expected_answer: The virtual DOM is an in-memory tree React diffs against the previous one to apply minimal real DOM updates. Fiber is React's reconciliation engine that splits rendering into units of work so it can pause, prioritise and resume.

common_mistakes: Saying the virtual DOM is always faster
questions.notes: Reported once in a secondhand account.

questions.prompt: Compare linear search and binary search. When is each suitable?
questions.relevance_to_role: A 2026 on-campus account lists linear versus binary search in the technical interview.
questions.expected_answer: Linear search scans in O(n) and works on unsorted data; binary search needs sorted data and takes O(log n).
common_mistakes: Using binary search on unsorted data
questions.notes: Reported once in a secondhand account.

questions.prompt: Explain Big O, Omega and Theta notation with an example.
questions.relevance_to_role: A 2026 on-campus account lists asymptotic notation in the technical interview.
questions.expected_answer: Big O is an upper bound, Omega a lower bound, Theta a tight bound. Example: linear search is O(n) in the worst case and Omega(1) in the best case (target is the first element); a loop that always runs n times is Theta(n).
common_mistakes: Using Big O for exact time
questions.notes: Reported once in a secondhand account.
